'''Kenneth John Falconer''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CBE|FRSE}} (born 25 January 1952) is a British [[mathematician]] working in [[mathematical analysis]] and in particular on [[fractal geometry]].<ref name="standrews">{{cite web | title=Kenneth Falconer's homepage at St Andrews University | url=http://www.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/~kenneth/ | access-date=1 July 2013 | archive-date=22 February 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190222094403/http://www.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/~kenneth/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> He is [[Regius Professor of Mathematics]] in the School of Mathematics and Statistics at the [[University of St Andrews]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Warrants Under the Royal Sign Manual: Regius Chair of Mathematics|newspaper=The Gazette|url=https://www.thegazette.co.uk/notice/2936539|date=22 December 2017}}</ref>

==Research==
Falconer is known for his work on the mathematics of [[fractals]] and in particular sets and measures arising from [[iterated function systems]], especially [[Self-similarity|self-similar]] and self-affine sets. Closely related is his research on [[Hausdorff dimension|Hausdorff]] and other [[fractal dimension]]s. He formulated ''[[Falconer's conjecture]]'' on the dimension of distance sets and conceived the notion of a [[digital sundial]].<ref name="standrews " /> In combinatorial geometry he established a lower bound of 5 for the [[Hadwiger-Nelson problem|chromatic number of the plane]] in the Lebesgue measurable case.

==Education and career==
Falconer was educated at [[Kingston Grammar School]], [[Kingston upon Thames]] and [[Corpus Christi College, Cambridge]]. He graduated in 1974 and completed his [[PhD]] in 1979 under the supervision of [[Hallard Croft]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |71337}}</ref>

He was a research fellow at [[Corpus Christi College, Cambridge]] from 1977 to 1980 before moving to [[Bristol University]]. He was appointed Professor of Pure Mathematics at the [[University of St Andrews]] in 1993 and was head of the School of Mathematics and Statistics from 2001 to 2004. He served on the council of the [[London Mathematical Society]] from 2000 to 2009 including as publications secretary from 2006 to 2009.<ref name="standrews" />

==Honours and awards==
Falconer was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 1998.

In 2020, he was awarded the [[Shephard Prize]] of the London Mathematical Society.<ref>{{Cite web|title=LMS Prize Winners 2020|publisher= London Mathematical Society|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news-entry/26062020-1657/lms-prize-winners-2020|access-date=2021-04-02}}</ref>

Falconer was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2024 New Year Honours]] for services to mathematics.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=64269|supp=y|page=N10|date=30 December 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Falconer was born 25 January 1952 at Bearsted Memorial Maternity Hospital outside [[Hampton Court Palace]].<ref name="standrews " /> 

His recreational interests include long-distance walking and hill walking. He was chair of the [[Long Distance Walkers Association]] from 2000 to 2003 and editor of their journal ''Strider'' from 1987 to 1992 and 2007–12.<ref name="Strider">{{cite magazine | title=40th Anniversary issue| magazine=Strider|publisher=Long Distance Walkers Association|date=September 2012|url=http://www.ldwa.org.uk/strider/public/40_anniversary/index.html#p=1}}</ref> In 2021, he was appointed a Vice President of the LDWA.<ref name="standrews" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=The Long Distance Walkers Association on Twitter|url=https://twitter.com/ldwa1/status/1368516378295173120|access-date=2021-04-02|via=Twitter|language=en}}</ref> He has twice climbed all the [[Munro]]s as well as all the [[Lists of mountains and hills in the British Isles|Corbetts]].<ref name="SMC">{{cite web | title=Scottish Mountaineering Club, Munro Compleatists | url=http://www.smc.org.uk/Munros/MunroistsCompleatists.php | access-date=1 July 2013 | archive-date=10 September 2009 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090910201702/http://www.smc.org.uk/Munros/Compleatists.php | url-status=dead }}</ref>
